reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows W addition improves dynamic plasticity and strength in TiZrMo-based HEAs, but these are different alloy systems (TiZrMo vs. HfZrTiTa0.53) and the W contents studied (8–18 at%) are higher than the proposed ~5 at%. The specific claim that ~5 at% W will form nanoscale precipitates and delay adiabatic shear banding in the HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy is not directly supported by the cited passages.
premises: W addition to refractory HEAs can improve dynamic plasticity and delay failure at high strain rates
W promotes a dual-phase microstructure with precipitates that enhance dislocation storage
W addition preserves or increases yield strength under dynamic loading
The base HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy suffers from limited strain hardening and rapid adiabatic shear banding
Microalloying with ~5 at% W will produce nanoscale W-rich precipitates in the HfZrTiTa0.53 system
